name: Waymo
sub: Robotaxi & passenger L4; Robotaxi consumer services
regions: United States; testing / planned UK and Japan
founded: 2009 as Google self-driving project; 2016 as Waymo
leadership: Tekedra Mawakana and Dmitri Dolgov, co-CEOs
about: Alphabet's robotaxi unit and the current scaled US commercial leader. They operate paid rider-only service and is expanding through both their own app and Uber in select markets.
model: Per-ride revenue via Waymo One and Uber integrations; potential licensing and logistics extensions
financing: Alphabet subsidiary; $16B investment round closed February 2026 at a $126B valuation (Sequoia, DST, Dragoneer joined), following the $5.6B 2024 Series C
investors: Alphabet; a16z, Fidelity, T. Rowe, Silver Lake, Mubadala
deployment: Phoenix, SF Bay Area, Los Angeles, Austin, Atlanta, Miami and Orlando open to the public; SFO airport service since January 2026; 2026 openings planned for Washington, Detroit, Las Vegas, San Diego, Denver, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio and Orlando; London confirmed as first international market, Tokyo in preparation with Nihon Kotsu and GO, and a German entity registered.
metrics: About 500k paid rides a week (mid-2026; sources range 400k-500k) across 11 US metros; fleet 3,067 per their December 2025 NHTSA filing, with press estimates of 3,000-4,000 since. $16B raised February 2026 at a $126B valuation. Sixth-generation Zeekr-built Ojai carrying public riders since 28 May 2026.
signal: Announced San Diego, Las Vegas, Tampa and Denver on 8 July 2026; freeway service suspended since 19 May 2026 pending a software fix, with a 3,871-vehicle recall filed 18 June.
